bib.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants

question: Can a benchmark of conceptually simple real-world assistant questions, hard for AI tools but easy for humans, measure general-assistant ability with simple automatic scoring?
hypothesis: Tasks that are conceptually simple for humans but need robust multi-step tool use are a better yardstick for general assistants than tasks that are ever harder for humans.
contributions: GAIA: 466 human-written questions with unique factoid answers, three difficulty levels
Question design and two-stage validation methodology
Evaluation of GPT-4 with and without plugins, GPT-4 Turbo, AutoGPT (GPT-4), a search engine and humans
Release of 166 annotated dev questions and 300 questions with held-out answers behind a leaderboard

method.summary: 466 questions written by compensated Surge AI annotators from author-made seeds, each answered by the creator and independently by two new annotators; questions kept if answers agree. Systems are prompted zero-shot with a format-fixing system prompt and scored by quasi exact match on the FINAL ANSWER.
method.task: general AI assistant question answering with web browsing, tool use, multi-modality and file reading

datasets.name: GAIA
datasets.split: 166 dev with annotations and answers; 300 with answers withheld for leaderboard
datasets.source: human-written by Surge AI annotators; Hugging Face gaia-benchmark
datasets.preprocessing: 623 newly crafted questions validated by two new annotators each; 68% valid as is, rest repaired or removed

other.selection: manual ChatGPT queries; Advanced Data Analysis mode or up to three third-party plugins chosen by authors per task (oracle)

inference.samples: APIs run three times, average reported; GPT4 + plugins single manual run; search engine and humans single
inference.prompting: zero-shot; system prompt fixes the FINAL ANSWER format (number, few words, or comma separated list; no units, articles, abbreviations)

other.timing: API times from running 20 questions then averaging

metrics.name: Score
metrics.definition: quasi exact match of FINAL ANSWER against single ground truth after normalization by answer type

eval.protocol: Automatic scoring function released with leaderboard; human score is fraction correct among validation annotators' attempts on valid questions; trace not evaluated

availability.data: 166 dev questions with answers, 300 without answers, leaderboard

prompts.text: You are a general AI assistant. I will ask you a question. Report your thoughts, and finish your answer with the following template: FINAL ANSWER: [YOUR FINAL ANSWER]. YOUR FINAL ANSWER should be a number OR as few words as possible OR a comma separated list of numbers and/or strings. If you are asked for a number, don't use comma to write your number neither use units such as $ or percent sign unless specified otherwise. If you are asked for a string, don't use articles, neither abbreviations (e.g. for cities), and write the digits in plain text unless specified otherwise. If you are asked for a comma separated list, apply the above rules depending of whether the element to be put in the list is a number or a string.

limits: Trace/plan is not evaluated, only final answer (Sec 6)
GPT-4 plugins score is an oracle: plugins hand-selected per question, manual ChatGPT queries, not reproducible; plugins change or disappear
AutoGPT underperformance may stem from its use of the GPT4 API (prompt and generation parameters); needs re-evaluation
OpenAI API gives no tool-call logs, so no fine-grained analysis; only strongest tool-capable LLMs evaluated
English only, annotators US-based; possible residual ambiguity; some questions unnaturally detailed
Few questions (466) vs MMLU ~15,000; benchmark will decay via contamination or web content disappearing
Levels are loose proxies from annotator step and tool counts, not hard constraints; no decoding parameters reported
Overall 15% for GPT-4 plugins appears only in abstract, not derivable from Table 4 without weighting
Dated: 2023 models; later systems have far higher scores (not in this source)

terms.definition: a t-AGI beats, on most tasks, most human experts who are given time t to perform the task
